queue.title: F272 -- settled: the lost terminal status row is the harness, not the product
queue.detail: DONE iteration 8. Two fixes. (a) LOAD AMPLIFICATION: four concurrent pytest processes, 6 rounds x 4 x 2 arms -- in-memory 5/24, file-backed 0/24, all five the identical output_recording.py:94 db.refresh -> InvalidRequestError traceback (p ~ 0.004). (b) DETERMINISTIC 2x2 over storage and pool, no product code: two sessions, A INSERTs, B close()s, A COMMITs. file + FORCED StaticPool loses the row; file + default QueuePool keeps it -- SAME STORAGE, opposite outcome, so the variable is the pool. engine.py:34-38 passes no poolclass and the dialect picks StaticPool (one connection per process) for :memory: and only for it; no shipped configuration has that. CORRECTION worth more than the verdict: both F272 and F266 said the write had 'already committed' -- it had not, the COMMIT commits an empty transaction because the INSERT was rolled back under it, so deleting db.refresh would HIDE a lost write. F266 settled by the same measurement (B->C, its bisection's unexplained 'load at full-suite scale' is exactly this, and now reproduces in 22s instead of 23min). F273 filed (B) for the one product-side residue: _execute_run's catch-all turns a failed terminal-status write into a log line. Repair candidates MEASURED: file-backed temp DB works but needs assert_engine_is_disposable rewritten; shared-cache + AsyncAdaptedQueuePool is right at the mechanism level and REFUTED at suite scale (8/8, sqlite_master locked, the app fixture's drop_all collides); file + forced StaticPool is 259s vs 4s. queue.title: Give the Hub suite per-session database connections without weakening the drop_all guard
queue.detail: AFTER p7-round, and NOT before the operator has seen decisions_for_user. The Hub suite runs sqlite+aiosqlite:///:memory:, which SQLAlchemy gives a StaticPool -- ONE DBAPI connection shared by every session in the process -- so any session's close() can ROLLBACK another session's uncommitted INSERT out from under its COMMIT. Measured under 4-way load at 5/24 on one test file; it is the cause of both F272 and F266 and is a live risk to any concurrent write in all 3849 tests, not just these. ONLY ONE CANDIDATE STANDS: a file-backed temp database (measured 0/24 under the same load). It requires re-expressing assert_engine_is_disposable (conftest.py:47-64), whose current rule is 'refuse to drop_all anything whose URL lacks :memory:' and which exists because a real operator database was destroyed -- that is the safety-critical part and the reason this is queued rather than done. RULED OUT, each by measurement, do not re-derive: shared-cache in-memory URL + explicit AsyncAdaptedQueuePool (right at the mechanism level, 8/8 failures at suite scale with OperationalError: database table is locked: sqlite_master, because the app fixture's drop_all/create_all collides with the other pooled connections holding the cache open); file + forced StaticPool (259s vs 4s for one 14-test file); shared-cache URL with no explicit pool (SQLAlchemy still picks StaticPool). Reproduction harness for any candidate: 4 concurrent pytest processes of hub/tests/test_a_turn_says_how_it_ended.py, 6 rounds, -p no:randomly, each run captured to its own file with --tb=long. An idle single-process loop measures 0/20 and is useless.

decisions_for_user.question: The Hub test suite's :memory: database gives every session ONE shared connection (SQLAlchemy StaticPool), which silently discards committed writes under concurrency -- measured 5 failures in 24 runs under load, and it is the cause of both F272 and F266. The only repair still standing is to run the suite on a file-backed temp database. That means rewriting assert_engine_is_disposable (hub/tests/conftest.py:47-64), whose current rule is 'refuse to drop_all any URL without :memory: in it' and which CLAUDE.md records as having been written after a real operator database was destroyed. The replacement rule would be 'refuse unless this suite created the file itself, under a temp directory'. Same purpose, different mechanism -- but the cost of getting it wrong is the same destroyed database. Confirm the guard may be re-expressed this way, or name the rule you want instead. Queued as f272-harness-repair; nothing will touch conftest.py until you answer. Everything else about F272 is settled and needs nothing from you.
